title: Algebraize a map to a scalar extension, with torsion kernel and cokernel
statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings and $R\to S$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $I\subseteq R$ be a finitely generated ideal such that the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism. Call an $R$-module $I$-power torsion when for every element $x$ there is an integer $n\geq0$ such that $r x=0$ for every $r\in I^n$; for an $S$-module use restriction of scalars. Let $P$ be an $R$-module and $Q$ an $S$-module; write $S\otimes_R P$ for scalar extension and $\psi_S$ for scalar extension of a linear map [def-weil-module-base-change]. For an $S$-linear map $\varphi:Q\to S\otimes_R P$ with $I$-power torsion kernel and cokernel, there exist an $R$-module $T$, an $R$-linear map $\psi:T\to P$, and an $S$-linear isomorphism $\beta:Q\to S\otimes_R T$ such that $\psi_S\circ\beta=\varphi$, and both $\ker\psi$ and $P/\operatorname{im}\psi$ are $I$-power torsion.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 0ALK (lemma-application-formal-glueing), proof of part (1), using Remark 05EL (remark-glueing-data) and Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence); torsion follows by exact localization and finite generation as in step 5 of lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-isogeny

proof.text: (Localizing a map with $I$-power torsion kernel and cokernel.) As $I$ is finitely generated, write $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$. Let $T$ be an $I$-power torsion $R$-module and $f=f_i$. For $x\in T$ pick $n\ge1$ with $I^nx=0$; then $f^nx=0$ since $f^n\in I^n$, so $x/1=0$ in $T_f$ and every element $x/f^e=(1/f^e)\cdot(x/1)$ of $T_f$ is $0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]: $T_f=0$. Now let $h:P\to Q$ be an $R$-linear map with $I$-power torsion kernel and cokernel. Localizing the exact sequences $0\to\operatorname{Ker}h\to P\xrightarrow{h}Q$ and $P\xrightarrow{h}Q\to\operatorname{Coker}h\to0$ at $f$ gives exact sequences $(\operatorname{Ker}h)_f\to P_f\xrightarrow{h_f}Q_f$ and $P_f\xrightarrow{h_f}Q_f\to(\operatorname{Coker}h)_f$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] whose outer terms are $0$; so $h_f$ is injective and surjective, an isomorphism. If $h$ is $S$-linear between $S$-modules, $h_f$ is $S$-linear, because the $S$-action on $P_f$, $Q_f$ is by the localized multiplications and $h_f\circ(s\cdot)_f=(h\circ s\cdot)_f=(s\cdot\circ h)_f=(s\cdot)_f\circ h_f$. In particular, in (1) and (2), $\varphi'_{f_i}$ is an $S$-linear isomorphism for every $i$.

proof.text: (Part (1): the glueing datum.) Use the category $\mathrm{Glue}=\mathrm{Glue}(R\to S,f_1,\dots,f_t)$ and the canonical maps $c^P_f$, $\sigma^P_{f,g}$ of [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], and the functor $\mathrm{Can}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence] (1): $\mathrm{Can}(N)=(N\otimes_RS,(N_{f_i}),(c^N_{f_i}),(\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}))$ is an object. Put $\mathbf D=(M',(N_{f_i})_i,(\alpha_i)_i,(\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j})_{i,j})$ with $\alpha_i=c^N_{f_i}\circ\varphi'_{f_i}:M'_{f_i}\to N_{f_i}\otimes_RS$, an $S$-linear isomorphism by step 1 and (1) of the proposition. $\mathbf D$ is an object of $\mathrm{Glue}$: condition (b) involves only the $N_{f_i}$ and $\sigma^N$, and is condition (b) for $\mathrm{Can}(N)$. For (a): localizing the identity $\sigma^{N\otimes S}_{f_i,f_j}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}=(\varphi'_{f_j})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{M'}_{f_i,f_j}$ (both send $(m/f_i^a)/f_j^b$ to $(\varphi'(m)/f_j^b)/f_i^a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]) and $(c\circ\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}=(c)_{f_j}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}$ (localization is compatible with composition), we get $(\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}\otimes S)\circ c^{N_{f_i}}_{f_j}\circ(\alpha_i)_{f_j}=(\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}\otimes S)\circ c^{N_{f_i}}_{f_j}\circ(c^N_{f_i})_{f_j}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}=c^{N_{f_j}}_{f_i}\circ(c^N_{f_j})_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{N\otimes S}_{f_i,f_j}\circ(\varphi'_{f_i})_{f_j}=c^{N_{f_j}}_{f_i}\circ(\alpha_j)_{f_i}\circ\sigma^{M'}_{f_i,f_j}$, using (a) for $\mathrm{Can}(N)$ in the middle. Moreover $\Phi=(\varphi',(\mathrm{id}_{N_{f_i}})_i):\mathbf D\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$ is a morphism of $\mathrm{Glue}$: $c^N_{f_i}\circ\varphi'_{f_i}=(\mathrm{id}\otimes_RS)\circ\alpha_i$ by definition of $\alpha_i$, and $\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}\circ\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}\circ\sigma^N_{f_i,f_j}$.

proof.text: (Part (1): conclusion.) By [prop-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-equivalence] (2) (essential surjectivity; its hypotheses are those of the lemma with $I=(f_1,\dots,f_t)$) there are an $R$-module $M$ and an isomorphism $\Theta=(\theta',(\theta_i)_i):\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathbf D$ in $\mathrm{Glue}$; since composition is componentwise [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data], $\theta':M\otimes_RS\to M'$ is an $S$-linear isomorphism and each $\theta_i:M_{f_i}\to N_{f_i}$ an isomorphism. The composite $\Phi\circ\Theta:\mathrm{Can}(M)\to\mathrm{Can}(N)$ (step 2) is, by full faithfulness in (2), equal to $\mathrm{Can}(\psi)=(\psi\otimes_RS,(\psi_{f_i})_i)$ for a (unique) $R$-linear $\psi:M\to N$. Comparing components: $\psi\otimes_RS=\varphi'\circ\theta'$ and $\psi_{f_i}=\theta_i$. Put $\beta=\theta'^{-1}:M'\to M\otimes_RS$; then $(\psi\otimes_RS)\circ\beta=\varphi'$, which is (1). Record also: $\psi_{f_i}$ is an isomorphism for every $i$.

proof.text: Let $K=\ker\psi$ and $C=\operatorname{coker}\psi$. The preceding algebraization step makes $\psi_{f_i}$ an isomorphism for every generator $f_i$ of $I$. Exact localization of the kernel and cokernel sequences [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] therefore gives $K_{f_i}=0$ and $C_{f_i}=0$. For $x$ in either module, the fraction equality criterion [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] gives a positive integer $e_i$ with $f_i^{e_i}x=0$. Put $e=1+\sum_i e_i$. The ideal $I^e$ is generated by monomials in the $f_i$ of total degree $e$. When the family is nonempty, such a monomial contains some $f_i$ to an exponent at least $e_i$, since otherwise its total degree is at most $\sum_i(e_i-1)<e$. It therefore annihilates $x$, and so does every element of $I^e$. When the family is empty, $I=0$ and $e=1$, hence $I^e=0$ also annihilates $x$. Thus $K$ and $C$ are $I$-power torsion.
